summary: The Isle of Man has no forced heirship, though a court may provide for family. Trusts are well established, the Hague Trusts Convention applies, and foundations are available.
family_claims: A family provision claim exists in Manx law; the statute was not identified.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables follow Manx law. There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: Hague Convention extended to the Isle of Man (1 January 1992 per a Dutch treaty record). Foundations Act 2011 allows private foundations.
open_questions: The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
Family provision statute and any remaining customary forced rules.
